note: Reviewed exceptions for record #8435 (controls that natively disable while their own write runs lose keyboard focus). node scripts/busy-control-inventory.mjs --check fails on any inventory candidate that is neither converted to a pending control nor listed here with the exact number found. Each entry: file, tag, the disabled expression exactly as the inventory prints it, count in that file, why it stays native, and the pull request whose review accepted it. Add an entry only for a control whose native state is a reviewed design, never to make the check pass.

The pending controls' own implementation: nativeDisabled is the caller's disabled (a permission or validation reason), held at its settled value while pending (usePendingDisabled), so a write in flight never disables the control natively.

The pending fields' own implementation (BusyInput, BusySelect, BusyTextarea): nativeDisabled is the caller's disabled, held at its settled value while pending (usePendingDisabled), so a write in flight never disables the field natively.

Not this control's own work: the help matcher opens only once the desk has loaded (a read the page starts, not this button). Opening the matcher starts no read or write.

Not a write state: unavailable is pending (the card is the Suspense fallback shown while the guide's code loads, a read the page starts, not this button) or loadFailed (the code failed to load and the card offers Reload). The loaded guide renders its own card without either, so no write of this button ever runs while it is disabled.

Not a write state: the live card's Done is disabled natively only while unavailable, which is pending (the Suspense fallback shown while the guide's code loads) or loadFailed (the code failed to load and the card offers Reload); the loaded guide renders its own card without either. Done's own write, the live acknowledgment, runs under pending={celebrating}, which keeps focus.

Validation, not a write state: canSubmit needs every answer, a current filer signature where one is required, the form still open here and its files available. The inventory links it to a busy name only through an unrelated id declaration elsewhere in the file. The submit itself runs under pending={busy}, and a newly unavailable submit applies only after pending ends.

Not this control's own write: filingBlocked holds Approve and Approve and open case while the filing readiness read loads or failed, the filer signature is missing, an attachment is stale or the sealed answers could not be opened (the same gate approve_form applies). The review's own writes run under pending={busy !== ""}.

Not this control's own request: Preview is natively unavailable while the draft is incomplete or while Send a test or Refresh runs. The panel runs one request at a time; while another control's request runs, focus is on that pending control, not this one. Its own request runs under pending={busy === "preview"}, which keeps it focusable while that request runs (usePendingDisabled holds its settled native state; tests/topic-update-panel.test.jsx).

Not this control's own request: Send a test to me is natively unavailable while the draft is incomplete, mail is not set up, or while Preview or Refresh runs. The panel runs one request at a time; while another control's request runs, focus is on that pending control, not this one. Its own request runs under pending={busy === "test"}, which keeps it focusable while that request runs (usePendingDisabled holds its settled native state; tests/topic-update-panel.test.jsx).

Starts no request: Send to N only opens the confirmation. It is natively unavailable until a delivered test of this exact text exists, and while Preview, Send a test or Refresh runs. The panel runs one request at a time; while another control's request runs, focus is on that pending control, not this one. The send itself is the confirmation's Yes, send it, a pending control.

Not this control's own request: Yes, send it and Refresh are each natively unavailable while the other panel request runs. The panel runs one request at a time; while another control's request runs, focus is on that pending control, not this one. Each one's own request runs under pending={busy === "send"} or pending={busy === "refresh"}, which keeps it focusable while that request runs (usePendingDisabled; tests/topic-update-panel.test.jsx).

Starts no request: the confirmation's Cancel only closes it. It is natively unavailable while Yes, send it runs, so the send cannot be abandoned mid-request; focus is then on Yes, send it, a pending control.

Starts no write: Invite the founder opens the form and Cancel closes it. Each is natively unavailable while another write on the same People waiting row runs (status, note, pass or the invitation itself). A row runs one write at a time; while another control's write runs, focus is on that pending control, not this one. The invitation's own write is Send founder invitation, a pending control (tests/people-waiting-busy-focus.test.jsx).

The validation reason keeps Send founder invitation focusable. This control is natively disabled during another write on the same row. Its own request uses pending={busy === "founder"} to keep focus on the submit button (tests/people-waiting-busy-focus.test.jsx).

entries.expression: {...mentionCandidates ? { role: "combobox", "aria-autocomplete": "list", "aria-expanded": mention.open, "aria-controls": mention.open ? `${threadDomId}-mentions` : undefined, "aria-activedescendant": mention.open ? `${threadDomId}-mention-${mention.sel}` : undefined, onKeyDown: mentionKeyDown, onClick: (event) => scanMention(event.target.value, event.target.selectionStart) } : {}}
entries.reason: A pass-through, not a write state: when mention suggestions exist the spread adds combobox ARIA attributes (role, aria-autocomplete, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant) and two handlers, onKeyDown (mentionKeyDown, which moves through and picks a suggestion) and onClick (which re-scans the draft for a mention). It never carries disabled, and the composer input has no disabled of its own.

entries.reason: Not this control's own write: checking belongs to the Revoke opener's read (set when Revoke is pressed, while focus is on Revoke), and the confirmation is natively unavailable only during that read. Pressing the confirmation sets verifying only in its fresh state, which makes it a pending control that keeps focus (pending={busy !== null || confirmOpen.verifying === true}); in its failed state the press starts the revoke write, which is pending too. Neither press returns it to checking.
